s: A poet's fortified summer house, built against Ottoman raids
w: Petar Hektorovic fortified his summer house in Stari Grad after Ottoman raids threatened Hvar in the 1500s, giving it a blank seaward facade. A seawater fish pool sits under a vaulted arcade inside, beside a dovecote tower and walled herb gardens. Its Croatian wall inscriptions rank among the oldest in the language.
_facts: Built by poet Petar Hektorovic (1487-1572) as a fortified Renaissance summer residence in Stari Grad
Long blank seaward facade for defense against Ottoman attacks; interior courtyard has a seawater fish pool under a vaulted arcade
Walled garden for medicinal herbs; wall inscriptions in Latin and Croatian rank among the oldest extant in the Croatian language

s: Called 'Hellish', but really named for pine tar
w: Locals call this scatter of islets off Hvar's harbour Skoji, but the popular name Pakleni is often translated as 'hellish.' It actually comes from paklina, an archaic word for the pine resin once harvested here and boiled into tar for caulking ships - a maritime trade, not a myth, behind the name.
_facts: Island group off the southwest coast of Hvar town, local name Skoji ('the islands')
Popular name 'Pakleni' is often mistranslated as 'hellish' but derives from paklina (pine tar/resin) once harvested and used to coat ship hulls

s: The cathedral that inherited a diocese from Stari Grad
w: St. Stephen's Cathedral closes off Hvar town's main square, seat of a diocese founded in 1147 after Venice conquered the island. The bishopric first sat in Stari Grad; as Venice built up Hvar town into the island's leading settlement, the seat moved here in 1278, and the cathedral has anchored the piazza ever since.
_facts: Roman Catholic cathedral of St. Stephen on Hvar's main square
Diocese of Hvar founded 1147 after the Venetian conquest of the island, originally seated at Stari Grad
Bishop's seat transferred from Stari Grad to Hvar town in 1278 as Venice developed Hvar into the island's chief town

s: A lighthouse islet guarding Hvar's harbour approach
w: A stone lighthouse has stood on this tiny islet, the easternmost of the Pakleni archipelago half a kilometre off Hvar town, since 1872. It guides vessels arriving from the open Adriatic into Hvar's harbour - a working aid to navigation on an island barely large enough to hold it.
_facts: Islet 500 metres south of Hvar town, easternmost of the Pakleni Islands
Lighthouse built in 1872 to guide ships arriving from the open sea into Hvar's harbour

s: A naturist islet, five minutes from Hvar by taxi boat
w: Five minutes by taxi boat from Hvar town, this pine-covered islet - barely a fifth of a square kilometre - has been a naturist getaway since the 1950s. Clear water and a scatter of restaurants draw day-trippers to what is otherwise one of the smallest of the Pakleni islands.
_facts: Islet in the Pakleni Islands, 0.207 square kilometres, five minutes from Hvar town by taxi boat
Naturist island since the 1950s, with pine trees and restaurants
